original_question: For an arbitrary Jordan pair V, determine the full normal subgroup structure of the projective elementary group PE(V); equivalently, classify all normal subgroups of PE(V).
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: the normal-structure (sandwich classification) problem for the projective elementary group PE(V) of a Jordan pair V, together with its equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main object, PE(V), and the fact that the paper is about describing its normal subgroups for a Jordan pair V. It also correctly treats the problem as a classification question about normal subgroup structure rather than, say, generators, presentations, or central extensions.
missing_details: The paper's target is not an unrestricted free-form classification of all normal subgroups; it is a specific ideal-theoretic sandwich description of normal subgroups.
The ambient base is a commutative unital ring k; the paper works with Jordan pairs over such a ring.
The statement is formulated using ideals I of the Jordan pair V, not just arbitrary subgroup-theoretic data.
The canonical quotient map pi_I: PE(V) -> PE(V/I), induced by the Jordan-pair quotient V -> V/I, is part of the statement and is absent from the draft.

The conjectural description includes both a lower bound and an upper bound for a normal subgroup N, namely a sandwich between a subgroup attached to I (naturally expressed via the quotient map) and the full preimage of the center of PE(V/I).
The ideal I is supposed to be unique; the draft omits this uniqueness.

The role of the center Z(PE(V/I)) is essential. The paper does not merely ask for a list of normal subgroups, but predicts that the only ambiguity above the ideal level comes from central factors in the quotient.
Proposition 1.2 gives an equivalent reformulation in terms of simplicity modulo center for simple Jordan pairs; that equivalence is missing from the draft.

Because the paper itself frames the problem as a conjecture plus an equivalent simpler-looking formulation, a stand-alone version should preserve that exact scope rather than broaden it to a generic 'classify all normal subgroups' question.
refined_question: Let V be a Jordan pair over a commutative unital ring k, and for each ideal I of V let pi_I: PE(V) -> PE(V/I) be the canonical homomorphism induced by the quotient V -> V/I. Is every normal subgroup N of PE(V) obtained from a unique ideal I of V by the sandwich condition ker(pi_I) <= N <= pi_I^{-1}(Z(PE(V/I)))? Equivalently, are the normal subgroups of PE(V) exactly those lying between the kernel of the natural quotient map to PE(V/I) and the full preimage of the center of PE(V/I), for a unique ideal I of V?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (as in Proposition 1.2), is it true that for every simple Jordan pair W, the quotient PE(W)/Z(PE(W)) is simple?
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at the paper's main normal-structure problem, but it is broader and less sharp than the paper's own formulation. Conjecture 1.1 is not merely 'classify normal subgroups of PE(V)'; it predicts a very specific classification controlled by ideals of V and by centers of quotient groups. Proposition 1.2 then reduces this to the corresponding simplicity-mod-center statement for simple Jordan pairs, which is the paper's official equivalent reformulation. That is why the refined question must mention the quotient map PE(V) -> PE(V/I), the unique ideal I, and the center of PE(V/I), rather than asking only for an abstract description of normal subgroups. Theorem 1.3 is part of the same introductory package of conjecture/equivalence/verified case that frames the paper's intent.
